newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish share extend gains, seen down on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish share extend gains, seen down on Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares extended Tuesday's slight gain but analysts said the stronger selling after price fixing and falls in continuous trade signalled a profit-taking fall on Thursday after recent sharp rises by small-cap stocks.
The overall market has flattened out over the past week after the previous 38-percent, large-cap-driven surge that started in mid-December.

"There have been big gains...and that's likely what led to selling today (after price fixing and in live trade) because the risk increases when firms grow so many times by the daily maximum," said Cezary Markiewicz of Bank Gdanski brokerage.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.7 percent to 18,251.3 points and turnover rose 28.2 percent to 250.4 million zlotys on both markets.
On Wednesday small-cap Olawa, Espebepe, Remak, Swarzedz and Paged all rose between 9.3 and 10 percent, with Espebepe's post-price-fixing buying strong enough to reduce players' bids.
Analysts said investors were likely speculating before the troubled firm's creditors meet on March 14.
Analysts said Prochnik would likely rise on Thursday after an owner's public tender call on Tuesday.
Prochnik trade was suspended on Wednesday, the day after National Investment Fund No.12 announced it would buy 343,501 shares at 11 zlotys, with the stock currently quoted at 9.7.
NFI units fell 0.6 percent in 35.2-million- zloty trade at the regular session and fell 1.2 percent in 24.7-million zloty continuous trade.

Analysts termed a good sign the Wednesday statement by new Finance Mininster Marek Belka that capital gains taxes on individuals would remain tax-free to 2000, but analysts did not expect a significant short-term effect on stock prices.
